evals.prompt: Run an accessibility audit on my plugin's dev site and fix whatever you find. The site runs at http://localhost:8765 via wp-env and .pa11yci.json is already set up at the project root.
evals.expected_output: A dry-run shown first (resolved binary, config, URL list), then `npx wp-tooling a11y --output json` executed with exit 3 treated as work-to-do. Violations grouped by id, ranked errors first, and the group list confirmed with the developer before any edit. Each fixed group is traced via domHints to the theme/plugin source, a diff is shown and approved before applying, and a re-run proves the id+selector pairs are gone. Final report includes before/after summary counts.
expectations: The skill runs `wp-tooling a11y --dry-run` and shows the resolved config and URLs before the real scan.
The scan uses `--output json` and exit code 3 is treated as violations-to-work-on, not a failure.
Violations are grouped by id and ranked by impact (errors before warnings; notices listed but not fixed unasked).
The developer confirms which groups to fix before any file is edited.
Source location uses domHints (idAttr, classList, attrs) to grep project source, not vendor/, node_modules/, or build output.
Every edit is shown as a diff and applied only after consent.
After each fix the skill re-runs the scan and verifies the specific id+selector pairs are gone.
The final report contains before/after summary counts and file:line for each fix.

evals.prompt: Check this project for accessibility issues.
evals.expected_output: The project has no pa11y config and no pa11y-ci installed, so the skill stops at preflight: it offers `npx wp-tooling add setup/pa11y` to scaffold .pa11yci.json and the pa11y-ci dev dependency, surfaces the npm install as a developer action, and does not run any package manager or invoke pa11y-ci by hand.
expectations: The skill detects the missing pa11y config / pa11y-ci during preflight rather than failing mid-run.
It offers the setup/pa11y scaffold as one way to get a config, not as a mandatory requirement.
It does NOT run npm install or composer require itself; installs are surfaced as developer actions.
It does NOT hand-roll a pa11y or pa11y-ci invocation to work around the missing setup.
If a config exists but the dev site is down, starting the environment is surfaced as a developer action or run only with consent.

evals.prompt: The a11y scan is failing on our WordPress site - can you sort out whatever it's complaining about? Config scans the front page, /wp-admin/ and /wp-login.php.
evals.expected_output: Violations on wp-login.php (WordPress core markup) are classified as upstream findings with suggested remedies (hooks/filters, upstream report) and are not patched in core or vendor code. Any URL with a scanError (e.g. connection refused) is treated as an environment problem - the skill checks the dev server rather than editing code. Project-owned violations follow the normal fix-with-consent loop.
expectations: Violations in markup rendered by WordPress core (wp-login.php) are classified as upstream and NOT fixed by editing core or vendor files.
Upstream findings appear in the report with suggested remedies instead of code patches.
A scanError entry (unreachable URL) is treated as an environment problem: the skill checks/starts the dev server, never edits code for it.
failedUrls > 0 with exit 1 does not get misreported as accessibility violations.
Project-owned violations still go through trace -> diff -> consent -> re-check.
The skill never adds pa11y ignore rules, drops URLs, or lowers the standard to make the run pass.

evals.prompt: The a11y scan reports: { "id": "WCAG2AA.Principle1.Guideline1_1.1_1_1.H37", "wcagCriterion": "1.1.1", "impact": "error", "message": "Img element missing an alt attribute.", "selector": "html > body > div.hero-banner > img", "context": "", "domHints": { "tagName": "img", "classList": ["hero-banner__image"], "idAttr": null, "attrs": { "src": "/wp-content/uploads/2024/hero.jpg" } } } at http://localhost:8888/. The theme has template-parts/hero.php rendering that exact markup. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The skill greps theme templates for the hero-banner__image class (domHints.classList), finds the in template-parts/hero.php, and proposes adding a real alt attribute (or an explicit alt="" if the image is decorative) rather than a placeholder. The diff is shown and applied only after consent, and a re-run confirms the WCAG2AA.Principle1.Guideline1_1.1_1_1.H37 id + the img selector are gone from the report.
expectations: The skill uses domHints (classList: hero-banner__image, tagName: img) to grep theme/plugin source, not vendor/, node_modules/, or build output.
template-parts/hero.php is identified as the render site for the failing .
The proposed fix adds a meaningful alt attribute, or an explicit alt="" with a stated reason if the image is decorative — not a placeholder like alt="image".
The diff is shown with file and line, and applied only after developer consent.
The re-run confirms the specific id + selector pair is gone, not just that overall violation counts dropped.
The skill does not suppress the finding with a pa11y ignore rule instead of fixing the markup.

evals.prompt:
The a11y scan reports a colour-contrast violation: { "id": "color-contrast", "wcagCriterion": null, "impact": "error", "runner": "axe", "message": "Element has insufficient color contrast of 1.65 (foreground color: #abb8c3, background color: #0693e3, font size: 12pt, font weight: normal): expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1", "selector": "div.wp-block-group > p", "context": "

Read more

", "domHints": { "tagName": "p", "classList": ["has-text-color", "has-background", "has-cyan-bluish-gray-color", "has-vivid-cyan-blue-background-color"], "idAttr": null, "attrs": {} } } at http://localhost:8888/. There's no hand-authored template with that class combination — the color comes from the Gutenberg block editor. The project's theme.json is attached.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes the has-*-color / has-*-background-color classes (inside a wp-block-group ancestor) as WordPress-generated Gutenberg block color-support markup, not a project-authored CSS class, so it does not grep theme PHP for that literal class string as if someone wrote it there. It traces the two color slugs (cyan-bluish-gray, vivid-cyan-blue) to their definitions in theme.json's settings.color.palette (#abb8c3 on #0693e3, ~1.65:1 — genuinely below the 4.5:1 requirement) and proposes adjusting that palette pairing (or the block's chosen colors) rather than inventing a new override class. The change is shown as a diff and applied only after consent, and a re-run confirms the color-contrast id + selector are gone.
expectations: domHints.classList containing wp-block-* / has-*-color / has-*-background-color utility classes is recognized as Gutenberg block color-support styling, not raw project-authored markup.
The skill does NOT grep theme/plugin PHP templates for the literal has-cyan-bluish-gray-color class string as if it were hand-authored there.
The fix is proposed at the level WordPress actually defines the palette (theme.json settings.color.palette, or the block's chosen color attributes) rather than a new ad-hoc CSS override class.
The change is shown as a diff and applied only after developer consent.
The re-run confirms the color-contrast id + selector pair is gone from the report.
The skill does not silence the finding by adding a class or style outside the project's existing block-color convention.
